exam.name: Claude Certified Developer – Foundations
exam.format: Multiple-choice and multiple-response items; each item states how many responses to select
exam.delivery: Pearson VUE — online proctored or at a test center
exam.passing: Scaled score of 720 on a scale of 100–1,000
exam.validity: 12 months from the date the credential is awarded
exam.reporting: Pass/fail with scaled score (100–1,000), plus percent-correct by domain on the score report
exam.retakes: Waiting periods of 14, 30 and 90 days after the 1st, 2nd and 3rd failed attempt; max. four attempts in a rolling twelve-month period; fee applies to each attempt
exam.renewal: Free on-time renewal via a non-proctored assessment on the Anthropic Partner Academy; a lapsed credential requires the full exam at the full fee

ui.heroEyebrow: Claude Certification Program · Exam Guide v1.0 · Effective July 2026 · Exam code CCDV-F
ui.heroTitle: Claude Certified Developer – Foundations: everything you need to pass.
ui.heroLead: A complete prep track built on the official blueprint: lessons for all 25 weighted skills, {questions} original exam-style questions, drill mode, flashcards, a diagnostic and timed 53-question mock exams scored on the 100–1,000 scale.
steps: Take the 24-question diagnostic to see which domains need the most work.
Work through the 25 lessons. Each ends with exam traps, practice questions and a build exercise.
Drill weak skills with instant feedback, and run flashcards daily for facts and numbers.
Sit full 53-question mocks under the 120-minute clock. Aim for 800+ consistently before booking.
ui.blueprintNote: Anthropic weights the 25 skills individually. A third of the exam sits in Applications and Integration; lessons and the question bank are sized by these weights.
ui.learnLead: The CCDV-F exam covers 8 domains and 25 individually weighted skills. Each lesson below maps 1:1 to a skill in the official Exam Guide v1.0 and is sized by its weight — spend your time accordingly.
ui.coverageNote: Every skill in the official Exam Guide v1.0 maps to one lesson. Question counts are sized by skill weight.
ui.recommendedOrder: Follow the numbering (1.1 → 8.3). Domain 2 builds on the API concepts you meet in Domain 1, and Domains 5–8 assume you can read a Messages API request. If you are short on time, prioritize by weight: 2.5, 2.4, 2.3, 5.2, 1.2, 5.1, 1.3, 6.2, 1.1, 8.1.

full.note: The real exam's format and pace (≈ 2 min 15 s per item). Use this for your final readiness checks.

ui.mockLead: Sit an exam-realistic simulation: questions are drawn in proportion to the 25 skill weights, options are shuffled, multiple-response items tell you how many to select, and there is no feedback until you submit. Scored on the 100–1,000 scale with 720 to pass.
ui.diagnosticLead: 24 questions in 45 minutes, sampled across all 8 domains in proportion to the blueprint. Take it before you start studying to find your weak areas, then again halfway through.
ui.exercisesLead: The Exam Guide recommends building and operating at least one Claude application that exercises the API, integrates tools, applies prompt and context engineering, and includes simple security and evaluation practices. Every lesson ends with a hands-on exercise; together they form that application.
ui.exercisesNote: The repository folder exercises/ contains tested reference implementations for the core exercises — agent loop (1.2/8.1), retry strategy (4.1), cost model (5.4), guardrail hook (7.3) and MCP server (8.2). Run python exercises/test_solutions.py (offline, no API key) to verify them.
ui.glossaryLead: terms from the Claude API, Agent SDK, Claude Code, MCP, LLM fundamentals and application security.

domains.name: Agents and Workflows
domains.summary: Decide between workflows and agents, construct agents with the Claude Agent SDK, custom loops or managed deployments, and apply common agent patterns and frameworks.

skills.name: Agent Architecture
skills.guide: Principles, patterns, and tradeoffs of agent and workflow architecture, including the decision criteria for using a workflow versus an agent, the structure of manager/supervisor hierarchies, and the role of subagents in improving task execution.

skills.name: Agent Construction with Claude
skills.guide: Methods, tools, and platforms for constructing Claude agents, including the Claude Agent SDK, custom agent loops and harnesses, managed agent deployment models (self-hosted vs. Anthropic-hosted), and hooks for deterministic actions.

skills.name: Agent Patterns and Frameworks
skills.guide: Common agent design patterns (tool-use loops, sub-agents, memory, context-window management) and agentic abstraction frameworks (e.g., Strands, LangGraph, PydanticAI) for building agents and workflows for multi-step tasks.

domains.name: Applications and Integration
domains.summary: The largest domain: requirements, life cycle, Claude API mechanics, software-engineering fundamentals, application design across Claude interfaces, and configuration management.

skills.name: Understanding Requirements
skills.guide: Functional and infrastructure requirements based on business requirements and solution architecture.

skills.name: Systems Life Cycle
skills.guide: Systems life cycle management concepts and frameworks used to develop, implement, operate, and maintain IT systems.

skills.name: Claude API Mechanics
skills.guide: Claude API behavior and mechanics, including messages, tools, streaming, vision, thinking, caching, invoking Claude through third-party vendors, Messages API data access patterns, batch API use, and tradeoffs between realtime and batch API selection.

skills.name: Software Engineering Foundations
skills.guide: Core software engineering principles and practices, including REST APIs, JSON, asynchronous programming, version control, SDLC integration, code review, and small- and large-scale refactoring.

skills.name: Claude Application Design
skills.guide: Design considerations for building Claude applications, including how Claude interprets instructions across interfaces (Claude Code, Desktop, claude.ai, API, SDKs), content boundaries, schema design, session hygiene, and plugin management.

skills.name: Configuration Management
skills.guide: Configuration management for Claude system components, including CLAUDE.md files, settings.json, model version pinning, prompt versioning, and plugin dependencies.

domains.name: Claude Code
domains.summary: Operate Claude Code: rules, skills, commands, subagents, memory, sessions, headless and streaming modes, auto mode, the CLAUDE.md hierarchy and settings.json.

skills.name: Claude Code Operation
skills.guide: Claude Code core components (Rules, Skills, Commands, Agents, Agent Memory), features (session management, built-in and custom slash commands, headless mode, streaming mode, auto-mode), the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, repository initialization, and settings.json configuration.

domains.name: Eval, Testing, and Debugging
domains.summary: Identify error types, choose recovery strategies, analyze traces to find failure modes, and isolate whether a problem originates in the integration layer or in model output.

skills.name: Debugging and Error Handling
skills.guide: Debugging and error handling techniques for Claude applications, including error type identification, recovery strategy selection, trace analysis to identify failure modes, and problem origin isolation between the integration layer and model output.

domains.name: Model Selection and Optimization
domains.summary: LLM fundamentals, technical integration fundamentals, choosing between Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, and managing tokens, caching and cost.

skills.name: LLM Fundamentals
skills.guide: Basic understanding of LLMs (tokens, context windows, sampling, non-determinism, next-token generation), model options (fast mode, extended thinking, adaptive thinking, effort levels), and fundamental prompting techniques (zero-shot, single-shot, multi-shot).

skills.name: Technical Fundamentals
skills.guide: Foundational technical concepts supporting AI application development, including basic engineering practices (integrating with SDKs that wrap REST APIs, websockets).

skills.name: Model Selection and Tradeoffs
skills.guide: Claude model capabilities (Opus vs. Sonnet vs. Haiku use cases, adaptive thinking support), tradeoffs across quality/latency/cost parameters, and breaking behavior changes across model releases when selecting models for tasks.

skills.name: Cost and Token Management
skills.guide: Token budgeting and cost management techniques for Claude applications, including token usage tracking, cost modeling, and caching techniques (prompt caching, cache check-pointing) for cost optimization.

domains.name: Prompt and Context Engineering
domains.summary: Manage context windows and prevent drift and bloat, write and iterate on prompts, and produce, validate and consume Claude output safely.

skills.name: Context Engineering
skills.guide: Context and memory management techniques for Claude applications, including context window management, prevention of context drift and bloat (tool output pruning, compaction), and context isolation through subagents or multi-step agentic workflows.

skills.name: Prompt Engineering
skills.guide: Prompt engineering principles and methods (instruction clarity, few-shot examples, system versus user placement, output constraints, prompt and instruction placement across components, iterative refinement, prompt adjustment, input sanitization) when writing and iterating on prompts for Claude.

skills.name: Output Handling
skills.guide: Established patterns and techniques for producing, validating, and consuming Claude output, including structured output patterns, response validation, defensive parsing, and skepticism toward confident output.

domains.name: Security and Safety
domains.summary: Defend against prompt injection and data leakage, layer guardrails, use hooks to stop destructive actions, and manage secrets and identities.

skills.name: AI Application Security
skills.guide: Data privacy and security best practices, including prompt injection awareness and mitigation, jailbreak defense, untrusted input handling, data leakage prevention, PII handling, and ensuring authentication, authorization, confidentiality, privacy, and integrity.

skills.name: Guardrails and Safe Deployment
skills.guide: Safe and responsible deployment practices (content policy, guardrail layering) and secure-by-design principles (privacy, identity and access management, least privilege).

skills.name: Claude Hooks
skills.guide: Leveraging hooks for guardrails and safety controls to prevent destructive actions within Claude applications.

skills.name: Identity, Secrets, and Key Management
skills.guide: Managing secrets, credentials, and API keys across Claude development and production environments, including identity validation and authentication, access approval and level verification, and authorized access monitoring.

domains.name: Tools and MCPs
domains.summary: Implement tools and function calling, build and integrate MCP servers, and choose between built-in tools, custom tools, Skills and MCPs.

skills.name: Tool Implementation
skills.guide: Tool implementation practices for Claude applications, including tool use and function calling, configuration for external system interaction, tool description writing, error handling, tool usage patterns (agentic harness dispatch, client-side vs. server-side tools, approval patterns), and tool set construction best practices.

skills.name: MCP Server Development
skills.guide: MCP server development practices, including server authoring, deployment, integration with Claude applications, MCP resources, tools, and prompts, and communication patterns (stdio, sockets, client vs. server).

skills.name: Agentic Customization
skills.guide: Tradeoffs among built-in Tools, custom Tools, Skills, and MCPs for selecting and applying the appropriate approach for a given use case.
